analysis.title: Global Rates Notes: 4Q26 Treasury Refunding Recap
key_insights: Treasury projects 4Q26 privately-held net marketable borrowing of $618bn (assuming an end-of-December cash balance of $850bn), vs GS expectation of $571bn. The figure was revised down $10bn from the August projection, mainly due to a higher beginning-of-quarter cash balance ($984bn actual vs $950bn projected in August), partly offset by lower projected net cash flows.

Treasury projects 1Q27 borrowing of $800bn assuming an end-of-March cash balance of $1tn, vs GS estimate of $713bn. The gap is almost entirely the higher TGA target (GS assumed $900bn), so the underlying borrowing pace is just barely below GS expectations.

Treasury kept nominal coupon, TIPS and FRN auction sizes unchanged but removed "at least" from its guidance that current sizes will remain for "at least the next several quarters." The TBAC minutes explicitly highlighted potential coupon auction changes in 2H27.
GS now expects coupon auction size increases to begin in August 2027, vs May 2027 previously. The later start is balanced by a wider scope.

GS now expects auction size increases in the 2-to-10y sector, vs 2-to-7y previously. Drivers are increased bank demand in the belly of the curve and weaker long-end demand from liability-driven investors.

GS baseline is unchanged long-end (20y and 30y) auction sizes, with risks skewed toward modest reductions. The TBAC minutes noted a "meaningful discussion" about potential changes, presumably downward, to 20y and 30y issuance at a later point.

Treasury cited growing private-sector and SOMA demand for bills. TBAC noted growing price sensitivity amid sluggish money market fund AUM growth. GS reads this as ongoing comfort with bill absorption.

Treasury expects $70bn of liquidity buybacks this quarter, keeping the upsized $6bn envelope for operations in the 10-to-20y and 20-to-30y buckets, and noted potential further enhancements. GS says the larger buyback envelopes and the focus on demand sensitivities should support spreads.

Treasury announced the conversion of the 7y note to a quarterly new issue, similar to 10y-30y. GS expects 7y auction sizes of $46bn / $43bn / $43bn across each quarter starting March 2027. Fewer CUSIPs should raise liquidity per issue.

TBAC discussed the implications of the AI buildout for Treasuries and noted no supply imbalances or absorption constraints. GS says this fits its finding that revised policy and growth expectations have been the main driver of higher yields this year.

Treasury again said shifts in its TGA path, including potential substantial intraquarter deviations from end-of-quarter assumptions, are driven by expected outflows, consistent with its cash balance policy.
